Short Description: Chicken braised in a sweet & savory spice paste, grilled over coals.
Main Ingredients: Chicken, sweet soy sauce, shallots, garlic, coriander
How to Make: Braise with spices till tender. Grill over charcoal, basting with soy sauce.
Philosophy & History: Caramelization over charcoal reflects Javanese patience for sweet results.
Local Etiquette: Best enjoyed muluk (bare hands) with warm rice, sambal, and raw greens.

Short Description: Whole chicken coated in spicy base genep, steamed or slow-roasted.
Main Ingredients: Chicken, base genep (shallots, ginger, turmeric, shrimp paste, lemongrass)
How to Make: Grind spices, coat and stuff chicken. Wrap in banana leaves; steam/slow-roast.
Philosophy & History: Originally for ceremonies. 'Betutu' refers to ancient slow-burning in rice husks.
Local Etiquette: Eaten communally (megibung). Meat is mixed with rice, satay, veggies, and sambal.

Short Description: Yellow-spiced chicken, crispy outside, juicy inside.
How to Make: Boil in yellow spices. Deep-fry until golden brown.
Philosophy & History: Ungkep technique is ancient Sundanese/Javanese wisdom using spices as natural preservatives.
Local Etiquette: Eaten with fingers. Soft bones chewed if free-range. Dipped in cooked sambal terasi.

Short Description: Minang-style boiled chicken, pale but incredibly savory.
Main Ingredients: Free-range chicken, coconut water, garlic, lime
How to Make: Boil in coconut water & garlic. Briefly dip (10s) in hot oil before serving.
Philosophy & History: Accidental creation in Bukittinggi. 'Pop' because it became highly 'Popular'.
Local Etiquette: Dipped lightly in mild tomato/chili sauce. Served with thin curry broth over rice.

Short Description: Chewy meatballs in a savory beef bone broth.
Main Ingredients: Ground beef, tapioca, garlic, beef bone broth
How to Make: Blend cold beef with ice, garlic, tapioca. Boil meatballs. Serve in marrow broth.
Philosophy & History: Adapted from Chinese pork meatballs (Bak-So) to Halal beef in the archipelago.
Local Etiquette: Customized at the table with soy sauce, sambal, vinegar. Noodles eaten with meat.

Short Description: Beef and offal soup with thick, roasted peanut-spiced broth.
Main Ingredients: Beef, offal, crushed roasted peanuts, lemongrass, galangal
How to Make: Boil meat with rice water (tajin). Sauté ground spices, add to the broth.
Philosophy & History: Tajin broth is ancient Bugis-Makassar ingenuity to thicken and remove gamey smells.
Local Etiquette: Eaten with halved ketupat or Burasa (coconut milk rice cakes), not plain rice.

Short Description: Broth soup with shredded meat, glass noodles, and veggies.
Main Ingredients: Meat, broth, turmeric, ginger, alliums, celery, glass noodles
How to Make: Boil chicken for broth. Sauté spices, add to boil. Shred chicken, serve with noodles.
Philosophy & History: Influenced by Chinese Caudo and Indian spices. Now has 70+ local variants.
Local Etiquette: Rice often mixed into the bowl. Garnished with lime, sambal, and crushed emping.

Short Description: Beef soup with pitch-black broth from kluwek nuts.
Main Ingredients: Beef, kluwek nuts, shallots, garlic, coriander, lemongrass
How to Make: Sauté spices with kluwek. Add beef and broth, cook slowly until pitch black.
Philosophy & History: Recorded in 901 AD Taji Inscription; one of Indonesia's oldest dishes.
Local Etiquette: Served with raw short bean sprouts, halved salted egg, and shrimp crackers.

Short Description: Chewy fried fish and sago cakes with sour-spicy-sweet cuko sauce.
Main Ingredients: Mackerel, sago flour. Cuko: palm sugar, tamarind, chili, garlic
How to Make: Knead fish with sago. Shape, boil, then fry. Serve with cuko.
Philosophy & History: Created in 16th century by an elderly Chinese man to preserve abundant fish catches.
Local Etiquette: Locals bite the pempek first, then slurp the cuko directly from a small bowl.

Short Description: Beef cooked slowly in coconut milk and spices until dry and preserved.
Main Ingredients: Beef, thick coconut milk, chili, galangal, ginger, turmeric
How to Make: Cook beef in coconut milk & spices. Stir slowly for hours until dry and caramelized.
Philosophy & History: Born from Minang migration tradition; preserved for long journeys. Crowned world's best food.
Local Etiquette: Eaten dry with warm rice. Leftover spice crumbs (dedak) are mixed with rice.

Short Description: Diced chicken skewers in thick, sweet, savory peanut sauce.
Main Ingredients: Chicken, peanut sauce, sweet soy sauce, shallots, lime
How to Make: Skewer and grill half-way. Dip in peanut sauce, grill fully. Serve with sauce.
Philosophy & History: Symbol of Madurese persistence; inspired by Arab Kebabs using local peanuts.
Local Etiquette: Meat pulled off with a fork. Plate wiped clean with crackers or lontong.

Short Description: Beef/tongue skewers in thick, spicy yellow/red sauce.
Main Ingredients: Beef tongue/meat, rice flour, turmeric, coriander, cumin, chili
How to Make: Boil meat in spicy herbs. Skewer and grill briefly. Thicken broth with rice flour.
Philosophy & History: 3 sauce colors (Yellow, Red, Brown) reflect Minangkabau flavor diversity.
Local Etiquette: Eaten on banana leaves with katupek, balado cassava chips, or beef skin crackers.

Short Description: Rice stir-fried in a hot wok with seasonings.
Main Ingredients: Firm white rice, sweet soy sauce, shallots, garlic, chili, egg
How to Make: Sauté spices, scramble egg. Add rice and soy sauce; mix on high heat (wok hei).
Philosophy & History: Originates from Asian philosophy of repurposing leftover cold rice to avoid waste.
Local Etiquette: Served with cucumber-carrot pickles as a palate cleanser and crackers.

Short Description: Young jackfruit cooked slow & sweet with coconut milk.
Main Ingredients: Young jackfruit, coconut milk, palm sugar, teak leaves
How to Make: Boil jackfruit, sugar, milk, teak leaves in clay pot on low heat for 12-24 hours.
Philosophy & History: Created in 16th century for workers clearing forests; cooked in large portions.
Local Etiquette: Served Pincuk style on banana leaves. Sweetness balanced with spicy beef skin stew.

Short Description: Nutrient-dense boiled veggies in thick peanut sauce.
Main Ingredients: Boiled veggies, tempeh/tofu, ground peanut sauce, palm sugar
How to Make: Boil veggies. Grind peanuts with shrimp paste, sugar, tamarind. Mix evenly.
Philosophy & History: Concocted by 17th-century soldiers mixing leftover peanuts with wild veggies.
Local Etiquette: Must be mixed evenly (digado) before eating with emping crackers.
